about.title: Oxnard Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Oxnard is a working city of roughly 207,000 people spread across Ventura County's coastal plain, and much of daily life happens on property someone else controls: grocery stores along Saviers Road, shops and lots off Oxnard Boulevard, apartment complexes near Rose Avenue, medical offices and strip centers along Ventura Road. When a floor is left slick, a walkway crumbles, or a railing gives way, the question under California premises liability law is not simply whether you fell. It is whether the owner or manager knew about the hazard, or should have known, and failed to fix it or warn you. That element, called notice, is where most Oxnard fall claims are won or lost. Evidence disappears quickly. Spills get mopped, store video is overwritten in days, and incident reports get filed away. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects you with an independent attorney who can send preservation letters, gather proof, and pursue your claim on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Oxnard Residents Use LawProactive After a Fall

items.title: Notice Has to Be Proven, Not Assumed
items.desc: California requires you to show the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney in our network knows how to look for cleaning logs, prior complaints and maintenance records that establish what the owner was aware of.

items.title: Deadlines Are Shorter Than People Expect
items.desc: You generally have two years to file a premises claim in California, but a fall on city, county or other public property in Oxnard triggers a much shorter government claim window. Getting connected early keeps every option open.

items.title: Surveillance Video Won't Wait
items.desc: Many Oxnard stores and complexes overwrite camera footage within days. An independent attorney can send a preservation demand right away, and California's pure comparative fault rule means a claim can still move forward even if you were partly to blame.

items.question: I slipped in a store off Saviers Road in Oxnard. What should I do first?
items.answer: Get medical care, then ask the store to write an incident report and give you a copy or at least a name. Photograph the spot, your shoes, and anything nearby such as missing warning cones or a leaking cooler. Names of witnesses matter too. The sooner an attorney requests the store's video and cleaning records, the better the chance that evidence still exists.

items.question: What if I was looking at my phone when I fell?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault, so your own share of responsibility reduces a recovery rather than erasing it. If a jury or adjuster decided you were 30 percent at fault, you could still pursue the remaining 70 percent from the property owner. An attorney can help you understand how that math might apply to your situation.

items.question: Does it matter if I fell on a public sidewalk or in a city park in Oxnard?
items.answer: Yes, quite a bit. Claims against a public entity such as the City of Oxnard or Ventura County require a formal government claim, usually within six months of the injury, before any lawsuit can be filed. That is far shorter than the two-year deadline for a claim against a private business or landlord. Because of that gap, it is worth speaking with an attorney quickly to confirm who actually controls the property.
